title: Adam Kadmon to Atzilus: the hidden called out, like a sign that reveals
overview:
Chapter 19 explains how the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* come out of *Adam Kadmon*: from its *Malchus* comes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*. The relationship is *gilui ha'helem*, the revelation of what is hidden, and it holds wherever a *yesh* of one world becomes the *ayin* of the next. Unlike *etzem v'hispashtus*, where something actually comes off the essence, here nothing is given: the essence is there, and a sign reveals it, as movement reveals life, words reveal thought and color reveals a ripe apple.

Rabbi Walters builds it on a person. An essential kindness shows itself through the wills it gives birth to, a separate will for each situation, by the associations of a self-image made in *Adam Kadmon*. The born will is never wanted for itself: bring the pizza and he never wanted to drive. So the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called lights, drawn off like Moshe's spirit onto the elders, and only the outer letters of each level, as the king's spoken wish becomes the servant's will, become the *Keser* of the next. *Kore hadoros meirosh*: the whole of history is called out of *Adam Kadmon*.

terms.gloss: revelation of what is hidden: nothing is given, the essence is there and a sign reveals it; the relationship of every yesh to the ayin below it
an essence and its spreading forth: something actually comes off the essence, like the energy of a throw or the sun's photons
the hidden sefiros: said plainly, the ten sefiros of Adam Kadmon
He calls the generations from the beginning: Adam Kadmon holds the picture of all history, and each generation is called out in its time
radiance: the light of an essence, which only reveals it
a sign: a thing not essentially connected to what it shows, but always associated with it
the essence of the attribute: the bias that gives birth to particular wills and is not separate from the person
a will for a will: the association in Adam Kadmon that ties a particular will to the essential will
subduing: making yourself do what you do not feel like doing, the naaseh that comes first
transforming: changing the way you look at a thing so that the feeling itself changes
the crowns: the Kesarim of the sefiros of Atzilus are revealed wills, compared to the hidden will of Adam Kadmon

sections.title: From Adam Kadmon to Atzilus: the hidden sefiros come out, like a flame from a coal
sections.summary: After the *igulim* and the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, the chapter explains how the lights of *Atzilus* come out of *Adam Kadmon*. Each world first defines what is wanted, then a picture of it, then how to do it; and the relationship between *Adam Kadmon* and *Atzilus*, as between any *yesh* and the *ayin* below it, is *gilui ha'helem* (the revelation of what is hidden).

phrases.he: (יט) ומעתה יש להבין בשרש עשר ספירות הנאצלים, ששרשם מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בשער הכללים דמבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר דעתיק יומין כו'

blocks.text:
Now we have to understand the root of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation): the *Etz Chaim* writes that *Malchus* (kingship) of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* (crown) of *Atik Yomin*.

After the *igulim* (circles) and *yosher* (straight line) of *Adam Kadmon* comes how the lights of *Atzilus* come out of it. Every world has lights like *igulim*, then a *yosher*, its *guf* (body); out of that body the light breaks through to the next world, into another body, down to *Asiya* (the world of Action). Each time it is abstract again, but more defined.

blocks.title: From a desire for a home to a house
blocks.text:
First a person has a desire for a home, which is just to feel a certain way. That becomes a desire for a house, already something concrete. So he defines what a house is, and from that he gets the basic building blocks he wants: a kitchen, a place that keeps him warm, all these things.

Then he pictures a dream house: one actual house, his wildest dream, but something he could in theory have physically. Then he figures out what is practical for him now, while still working toward the higher one, then how to get that, and he keeps cutting it down until he knows what to do right now. Each time it goes abstract, then needs a concrete form, and each time it is cut down to be more particular.

In general there are three stages, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* (the three lower worlds). They happen in the *ratzon* (will) and again in action: three to figure out what you want, three to figure out how to get it. The *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) in the will, down to the end of *Atzilus*, is figuring out what you want: your essential will gets an essential definition, then a picture of how it could be done, then how to bring it about.

blocks.title: The house in Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya
blocks.text: That is the general *mashal* (analogy) for *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*: a person making a house. In *Beriya* he makes the plan: doors and windows, this room and that room, the abstract definition of what makes up a house. In *Yetzira* he pictures how they will be made: "Well, what am I going to build it out of, wood or stone or brick, and what shape is it going to be?" In *Asiya* he figures out how to build that form.

Until modern times they could not build very large rooms; the materials were not strong enough. Then came the dome, then pillars and other methods, and now steel I-beams make really big rooms. The skeleton of a building today is beams shaped like an uppercase I: two parallel pieces of metal joined in the middle. A solid block sags under its own weight; the I is the strongest shape relative to its weight, so it does not weigh itself down. All these innovations let them practically build it. Sometimes an architect makes a very nice design that the construction crew can hardly make.

But you also need those three stages in your will. In *Adam Kadmon*, say you want to be happy: first you have to figure out, well, who am I? What are the essential needs of a person like me, the needs that have to be filled to make me happy?

blocks.title: Morality in schools
blocks.text: There are the basic needs. A government system works this way too: first it figures out the basics, life and liberty and all those things. He was thinking about this because he was listening to a *sicha* (talk) in which the Rebbe complained that in the name of liberty they do not teach children morality in schools, because of the separation of church and state. The real problem is that religion is a higher *masach* (interface) than the government.

sensitivity.reason: Reports the Rebbe's complaint that, because of the separation of church and state, schools teach no morality: a stand on an American political dispute.
sensitivity.publishable: There are the basic needs. A government system works this way too: first it figures out the basics, life and liberty and all those things. He was thinking about this because he was listening to a *sicha* (talk) in which the Rebbe spoke about teaching children morality in schools. The real problem is that religion is a higher *masach* (interface) than the government.

blocks.text: If you change the definition on a higher level, that automatically changes everything on the lower levels. Change *Adam Kadmon*, and the way you react to the same information is totally different. So it is impossible to build something except from the foundation.

So a government system that ignores religion is impossible: it will not set the ultimate goal, and without one there is no standard to measure decisions on. It takes time to become an issue, but eventually it breaks down. Even with a separation of church and state, everybody has to agree on certain common goals the government will uphold, even if they are not their religion's: some utopian state it is trying to achieve. Without an ultimate goal you cannot make any judgment, because you do not know where you are going; when a dispute comes up, there is no way to decide.

sensitivity.reason: Says a government that ignores religion will break down: a political opinion on church and state.
sensitivity.publishable: Without an ultimate goal there is no standard to measure decisions on. It takes time to become an issue, but eventually it breaks down. Any group has to agree on certain common goals, a picture of what it is trying to achieve. Without an ultimate goal you cannot make any judgment, because you do not know where you are going; when a dispute comes up, there is no way to decide.

phrases.he: והנה תחלה יש להקדים בענין עשר ספירות הגנוזות בהעלם,
איך שיוצאים לידי גלוי
phrases.en: How they come, how they're revealed.

phrases.he: שזהו מה שכתוב קורא הדורות מראש,
phrases.en: It says that *Hashem* calls out the generations, meaning everything that's going to happen in history,

phrases.he: מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: *Hashem* calls out from *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: Now, how it goes from *Adam Kadmon* to *Atzilus*. First we have to preface the ten hidden *sefiros*, how they come out into revelation. The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* are called the *sefiros hagenuzos* (the hidden sefiros). The *sefiros* before the *tzimtzum* (contraction) are also called *genuzos b'helem ha'Atzmus*, hidden in the concealment of the Essence, but *genuzos* plain means those of *Adam Kadmon*. **How they come, how they're revealed**: the relationship this chapter explains is called *gilui ha'helem* (the revelation of what is hidden).

The *hishtalshelus* has two general kinds of relationship: *gilui ha'helem*, and *etzem v'hispashtus*, an essence and its spreading forth. Here it is *gilui ha'helem*. It is explained about *Adam Kadmon* and *Atzilus*, but on every level, whenever you go from a *yesh* (something) to an *ayin* (nothing), from an *etzem* (essence) to an *or* (light), from a *Maor* (source of light) to a light, from the *yesh* of one world to the *ayin* of the world under it, it is a *gilui ha'helem*.

That is the verse *kore hadoros meirosh* (He calls the generations from the beginning): from the *rosh* (head) of *Adam Kadmon*. **It says that *Hashem* calls out the generations, meaning everything that's going to happen in history**. *Adam Kadmon* is the whole picture of everybody and everything that will happen, and every generation *Hashem* calls out, "Okay, it's time for you guys to come out," and they come down to the world.

phrases.he: ואמר בספר יצירה
שזהו כשלהבת הקשורה בגחלת,
phrases.en: that this is like the relationship of a fire the way that it's inside of a coal

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא יש דמיונות רבים
phrases.en: there's many other types of examples for this thing.

blocks.title: The flame hidden in the coal
blocks.text: The *Sefer Yetzira* (the Book of Formation) says it is **like the relationship of a fire the way that it's inside of a coal**. In a coal the fire is hidden; blow on it and it comes out *b'gilui* (revealed). It comes out because it really is on fire. **There's many other types of examples for this thing**: it was really there, and now it is just coming out *b'gilui*.

sections.title: Revealing the hidden is not spreading forth: the sign, not the thing
sections.summary: In *etzem v'hispashtus* something actually comes off the essence, like a thrown stone's energy or the sun's photons. In *gilui ha'helem* nothing is given: the essence is there, and the better the vessel, the more of it shows, as movement shows life and words show thought, a sign with no essential connection to what it reveals.

phrases.he: ויובן יותר מי' כחות הנפש
phrases.en: but we'll understand it better from a *mashal* in ourself, from the ten powers of the soul.

phrases.he: דהנה ידוע ענין העלם וגלוי אינו כהתפשטות כח מן העצם,
phrases.en: That *helem* and *gilui* are not the same as *hispashtus* from an *etzem*.

phrases.he: כמו כח הפועל שמתפשט בפעולה,
phrases.en: like when you throw something.

phrases.he: שזהו מהות כח העצם שנקרא עילה ועלול
אלא כמו בחינת זיו ואור של העצם
phrases.en: but rather it's like the *ziv* and the *or* of the *etzem*,

phrases.he: כהארת זיו אור השמש, וכחיות אור הנפש בכלי הגוף, וכהתחכמות מכח השכל וכהאי גוונא
והיותר דמיון אמיתי לגלוי ההעלם הוא כמו גלוי התנועה מן החי
phrases.en: is like the *gilui hatenua min hachai*: in other words, when something is moving, that shows you that it's alive.

phrases.he: וכאותיות המחשבה ואותיות הדיבור
phrases.en: like when you talk, your *osios hadibur* reveal what you're thinking.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: **But we'll understand it better from a *mashal* in ourself, from the ten powers of the soul.** It is known **that *helem* and *gilui* are not the same as *hispashtus* from an *etzem***, as the power of the doer spreads into the deed, **like when you throw something**: you actually expend effort, you put energy into it. That is *ila v'alul* (cause and effect).

**But rather it's like the *ziv* and the *or* of the *etzem*** (its radiance and its light): like the shining of the sun's light, the life of the soul's light in the vessels of the body, and the insight that comes from the power of the intellect. And a truer likeness of *gilui ha'helem* is the revealing of movement from a living thing, and the letters of thought and the letters of speech. So these are all *meshalim* (analogies).

Really everything has both *etzem v'hispashtus* and *gilui v'helem*. Earlier he gave four *meshalim* for *etzem v'hispashtus*: the light of the sun, the light of a candle, the soul coming into the body, and the power of movement in throwing. When you throw, you put energy into it. A candle's fire actually burns something up, and the light is something coming off. The sun's light too is a *yesh*, a something, coming out.

*Gilui v'helem* means that you are not being given something. The *etzem* is there, and it is only a question of how much you are able to appreciate what is there: that is how much you will see of it.

blocks.title: Exercise and the stronger body
blocks.text: The body's *chayus* (life) has both. When a person exercises, the energy he puts into what he throws is *etzem v'hispashtus*: he actually expends it. But afterwards he is stronger. Why? His body has become a better vessel for his soul, more refined, more efficient. The soul has the same abilities; the body can now be *megaleh* (reveal) more of it.

blocks.title: Light in the room, the sun through the window
blocks.text: The same in the sun's light. The light that comes off is *etzem v'hispashtus*: when it comes through your window and just makes your room light, you see the light as it is, separate from the sun. But look through the window and the light disappears and you see the sun, its form; the light only reveals what is there. That is *gilui v'helem*. Both are going on.

blocks.title: The eye and the ear
blocks.text: The same with the life of the soul in the vessels of the body. The power of consciousness goes into the eye, a vessel that lets it see. The soul is a simple essence; the eye lets it reveal only sight, the ear only hearing. A healthy body expresses the soul well. That is *gilui v'helem*: the better the vessel, the more light it gets. The soul is not giving more; the vessel receives it better, is more transparent to it.

Or the insight of the intellect. When a teacher explains something, all he is really doing is helping you look the right way, so you see something already there; and when you study, you are setting yourself up to perceive. That is why the baby is taught the whole Torah before it is born: the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight) means you really perceive the whole truth. What you do not see is how it applies here. For that you need *iyun* (close analysis) and study, and then the inner perception is revealed in your brain in this instance. The more you refine your brain, the more it comes in.

The photons that come out of the sun are an actual *hispashtus*: they were in the sun and now are here; the sun is losing something. That is a physical *shefa* (flow), not really *or*. But the photons are ready to take any form: whatever they hit they bounce off, and when they hit your eye you see the thing. That is *gilui ha'helem*. What *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) calls *or* is not the physical light but the revealing of the thing.

This *gilui ha'helem* is the main thing he is explaining here, and these are all *meshalim* for it; soon he gives its main idea. Some of the same *meshalim* are also used for *etzem v'hispashtus*: one aspect of light is a *mashal* for *etzem v'hispashtus*, another for *gilui ha'helem*, and the same with the soul.

He talked about this a little earlier, and it is explained at length elsewhere: in the *maamar* (discourse) *Sachar Oscha* in the *Siddur*, on which Reb Hillel bases his commentary here, and, he thinks, in quite a number of *maamarim* at the beginning of *Ayin Beis* (the Rebbe Rashab's series of discourses), based on the explanation in *Imrei Bina* of the difference.

Getting more particular, there is *etzem v'hispashtus* in *ruchni* (spiritual) and in *gashmi* (physical), *gilui ha'helem*, *hislabshus* (enclothing): particulars within the two general categories. *Chassidus* explains the difference between them because different parts of the *hishtalshelus* correspond to them. To understand the whole *hishtalshelus* properly, you have to understand all of them.

blocks.title: Even a vulture knows
blocks.text: A truer likeness of *gilui ha'helem* **is like the *gilui hatenua min hachai*: in other words, when something is moving, that shows you that it's alive.** You do not see the life itself, "but everybody knows, like even a vulture knows" that when somebody stops moving he is dead. Wire it up and shock it and it moves, but it is not alive. Movement is just a *siman* (sign) that it is alive.

blocks.title: Go three blocks and make a left
blocks.text: And the letters of thought and speech: **like when you talk, your *osios hadibur* reveal what you're thinking.** The sounds are not the thought; once you know the language, this word means that. A guy giving directions says, "Go three blocks and make a left at the light," and as soon as you hear the sounds you conjure a mental picture. All you got was sounds; in another language you would have no idea, because the sounds have no essential connection to what they reveal.

phrases.he: וכל זה יותר אמיתי מדמיון שלהבת הקשורה בהעלם בגחלת
phrases.en: And all of these are a better *mashal* than the fire that's inside the coal.

phrases.he: שאף על פי שבגחלת היה השלהבת בהעלם,
phrases.en: even though in the coal the fire was hidden,

phrases.he: אבל הרי על כל פנים ממהות חום שבגחלת יצא השלהבת,
phrases.en: but the coal's actually on fire,

phrases.he: ואין זה אמיתית ענין הגלוי
רק כמו בחינת מראה וגוון לבד,
phrases.en: The real *inyan* of a *gilui* from a *helem* means like an appearance or like a color,

phrases.he: כגוון התפוח
phrases.en: like an apple.

phrases.he: שאינו ממהות התפוח,
phrases.en: The color is not the actual *mahus hatapuach*.

phrases.he: וכידוע

blocks.text: **And all of these are a better *mashal* than the fire that's inside the coal**: **even though in the coal the fire was hidden** and blowing reveals it, the flame still came out of the coal's heat. **The coal's actually on fire**: not a flame, just a hot burning, but something is going on. The flame is the gas released by the burning getting hot and ionized, which gives off light. So there is a direct connection.

So in a way it is *etzem v'hispashtus* from the fire, which gives off the heat. That the flame gives off light only lets you know something is burning; the light is not the fire. That is the *gilui ha'helem* part: "when there's smoke there's fire." The light is not the burning itself. Rust is the same thing as fire going very slowly, an explosion the same thing going very quickly; fast enough, it makes a flame, it makes light.

blocks.title: The color of the apple
blocks.text:
And this is not the true meaning of a *gilui*. **The real *inyan* of a *gilui* from a *helem* means like an appearance or like a color**, **like an apple**. A nice red outside lets you know it is ripe; green, it is not. The color is not the ripeness, just a sign of it. Cut it open: white, it is sweet; brown, it is spoiling. But the white is not the sweetness. Paint a rotten apple white and it will not taste good. "That's not the way it works."

**The color is not the actual *mahus hatapuach*** (what the apple is in itself). G-d just made apples look like this when ripe and like that when not. They are not essentially connected, but since *Hashem* made them always go together, one is a *siman* of the other: a sure sign, a symptom.

sections.title: The attribute shows through the will it gives birth to
sections.summary: A person's essential kindness or cruelty is hidden; it is revealed by the wills and opinions it always produces. The source of those wills, the bias itself, is still the essence, but each particular will is only a sign, like movement revealing life, and a single deed cannot be judged without the whole picture.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בגלוי העלם עצם כחות הנפש,
phrases.en: Same way with the *etzem hanefesh*, its *kochos* are revealed,

phrases.he: כמו כח מדת החסד בעצם
שגלוי שלו היינו כאשר מצד עצמיות מדה זו בעצם הנפש, הרי מתהווה רצון ושכל של חסד וטוב תמיד
ולהיפך במי שמדתו העצמית באכזריות,
phrases.en: somebody that's cruel,

phrases.he: מתהווה רצון ושכל לדין ועונש

blocks.text:
**Same way with the *etzem hanefesh*, its *kochos* are revealed** (the essence of the soul and its powers), as with kindness in the essence: when this attribute stirs in the soul, a will and an intellect for kindness and goodness always come into being.

"How do you know that I'm a nice guy?" "Because you always want to do nice things, and whenever somebody asks your opinion about something, you lean towards *chesed* (kindness)."

It is like when they call somebody a liberal. What do you mean, he is a liberal? How do you know what he is in his inner self? "Because I see that whenever a question comes up, he always leans towards *chesed*, or whatever, that side."

sensitivity.reason: Uses a political label (a liberal) as the example of a person who leans toward kindness.
sensitivity.publishable: It is like when people say of somebody that he is soft-hearted. What do you mean? How do you know what he is in his inner self? "Because I see that whenever a question comes up, he always leans towards *chesed*, or whatever, that side."

blocks.text: And the opposite, **somebody that's cruel**. They call Hitler, may his name be erased, a monster. "How do you know what he was on the inside?" From what he always wanted to do, how he looked at things, what he said. That is only a *gilui*: you do not see his feelings and personality, but it reveals them. An essentially cruel person always reveals it as a bias: his will and *sechel* (intellect) lean towards judging, punishing, being cruel.

phrases.he: והנה התהוות מקור לרצון זה, לחסד או לדין, נחשב עדיין מעצם המדה,
phrases.en: the fact that he has a bias that leans towards this thing, that is still considered the essence,

phrases.he: שאינו נבדל הימנה כלל

blocks.text: The coming into being of the source of this will, for kindness or for judgement: **the fact that he has a bias that leans towards this thing, that is still considered the essence**, not separate from it at all. The creation of that source of all these particular desires is part of who he is; that is his inner *ratzon*.

phrases.he: אבל מה שנולד רצון בגלוי לדין או להיפוכו,
זהו רק כמו בחינת התגלות מראה לעצם
phrases.en: This is only like a color that's revealing the essence.

phrases.he: כהתגלות התנועה בעצם החי
phrases.en: like the movement that shows that something's alive.

phrases.he: וכגלוי החיות בדבר נבדל, שהוא הגוף
phrases.en: the *gilui hachayus* means the consciousness.

phrases.he: שמפני שהוא חי בעצם,
phrases.en: since the soul is essentially alive,

phrases.he: מגלה חיותו בתנועה
phrases.en: it reveals the fact that it's alive by moving the body.

phrases.he: וכן מפני שהוא דבר חי בעצם,
phrases.en: and since the soul essentially has a consciousness,

phrases.he: מחיה גם לגוף הדומם
phrases.en: it also has physical perception when it's in the body,

phrases.he: שנקרא חיי בשר כו'
phrases.en: which is called physical life.

blocks.text: But the will that is born revealed, for judgement or the opposite: **this is only like a color that's revealing the essence**, like movement revealing life. A person's particular actions are a sign of where his sympathies lie; he shows his true colors. Watch him in different situations and you gather his priorities and figure out his personality. "It's impossible really for a person to hide himself": whatever he wants comes through in how he reacts.

blocks.title: The man tied to a bench
blocks.text: On the other hand, you cannot judge somebody just from what he did, without a big picture for reference. Say I tell you a guy tied somebody down to a bench and cut him up. Nice guy or mean guy? That is not enough information. The action itself is not a sure sign, and to think that whoever does it necessarily means this is incorrect.

That leads to a lot of judging people and a lot of unnecessary hatred. A person knows what the action would mean coming from where he comes from, with his background, culture and motives. But for this person, unless you know where he is coming from, you need a bigger picture before you can judge what it means for him. Like a word: even knowing its definition, without its context and tone of voice you will not necessarily know what it means.

To the point that a person could do what the Torah calls a sin and really be expressing his desire to connect to G-d, if he was misled: a *tinok shenishba* (a child taken captive, raised without Torah) told that this is how to connect to G-d expresses a good thing the wrong way. Like a person who uses a word wrongly because he does not know what it means: from the context you figure out what he means.

That is the general idea of *gilui ha'helem*: something that is essentially not connected, once it becomes associated, reveals the essence. The essential bias, the fact that he will always look to *chesed*, is from the essence; the particular things he does are not. Therefore a person can do things that are outwardly *gevura'dik* (stern) because of a motivation of *chesed*.

In educating a child, a parent or teacher very often has to be strict, outwardly the opposite of what they want. But as the Rebbe Rashab says in *Chinuch Lanaar*, if you consistently mean the child's best, he will sense it and respond positively; if you do not, he will notice that too, and he will not want to listen.

One of the main things is a double standard: the child is told something is good to do, and then the parents do not want to do it. The parent may mean well, but it will not have much effect. Like they say, parents who tell their kids not to do what they did have kids who tell their kids not to do what they did. When guests come and the kids are expected to give things up, the parents could be doing what they themselves think is right and want to teach, or sparing themselves discomfort by making the kids do it. Then the kids resent it. If they see the parents doing it themselves, they appreciate it and learn to be kind.

The next class reads it again: the will born revealed is only like the revealing of an appearance of the essence, **like the movement that shows that something's alive**. The movement is not the life: make something move and it is not alive, not at all. But if something is alive, it is going to move.

blocks.title: Is the baby blind or deaf?
blocks.text: And the revealing of life in a separate thing, the body: **the *gilui hachayus* means the consciousness**. How do you know a person has a conscious soul? His eyes follow you when you move in front of him. How do they know if a baby is blind or deaf? Clap next to its ear and it does not respond; pour water over its eye and it does not shut it; wave something in front of its face and it does not flinch. The physical responses show whether it has a spiritual consciousness of those things.

**Since the soul is essentially alive**, **it reveals the fact that it's alive by moving the body.** **And since the soul essentially has a consciousness**, **it also has physical perception when it's in the body**, **which is called physical life.**

phrases.he: כי גלוי רצון זה בא בדבר נבדל, שהוא ענין זה של חסד או דין
אבל מקור המוליד רצון זה
הוא בא מכח עצם המדה לבד
phrases.en: it only comes from *etzem hamidda*

blocks.text: For the revealing of this will comes in a separate thing. As with the soul: that it can move things, control things, be conscious of things is from its essence; whether this is revealed in the body is not. So too the will that comes out: **it only comes from *etzem hamidda*** (the essence of the attribute), but it is not *etzem hamidda* itself.

sections.title: One source, many wills: the born will is not what you really want
sections.summary: One essential attribute gives birth to a separate will for each situation, through the associations made in *Adam Kadmon*. The born will was never wanted for itself: take away its connection and it vanishes, which is why the world is *yesh me'ayin*, and why prayer must lead the animal soul back to what it really wants.

phrases.he: ומובן ממילא, בהיות שיש כמה אופני דברים שיוליד רצון מיוחד לכל אחד ממקור אחד,
phrases.en: And so it's understood that in many different *retzonos*, each one will have its own *ratzon*, but they're all coming from one *makor*.

phrases.he: שהוא תלוי בעצם המדה תמיד כו'
וגם שכל המטה תמיד כלפי רצון וחסד, היינו רק מצד עצם מדת החסד
phrases.en: the fact that a person is always biased towards *chesed* is because they have an essential kind nature

phrases.he: שמוליד תמיד רצון ושכל לחסד דוקא
ויש כמה ענינים נבדלים
phrases.en: but there are many different things that this will be expressed,

phrases.he: ולכל אחד מוליד רצון ושכל בפני עצמו כו'
phrases.en: and this essential *midda* will create an individual *ratzon* for each scenario.

phrases.he: ודי למבין

blocks.text: **And so it's understood that in many different *retzonos*, each one will have its own *ratzon*, but they're all coming from one *makor*** (source), which always depends on the essence of the attribute. An essentially nice person wants many different things to express that *midda* (attribute), as each situation calls for, sometimes in a way you would associate with *gevura* (might, restraint), like a surgeon.

And an intellect that always leans towards kindness is only from the essence of kindness. **The fact that a person is always biased towards *chesed* is because they have an essential kind nature.** His constant particular wills for *chesed* are a sign of it. **But there are many different things that this will be expressed**, **and this essential *midda* will create an individual *ratzon* for each scenario.**

This is what *Adam Kadmon* does: it connects the essential *middos*, its *igulim*, with the particular wills of *Atzilus*. Those are not the essential will. A will to cut somebody is a particular will; whether it is *chesed* or *din* (judgement) you cannot tell unless you see how it is associated. That association, what will accomplish what, is made in *Adam Kadmon*: a person makes a self-image and a worldview, so he knows that in this situation his essential desire for *chesed* is expressed like this, and his desire for *gevura* like that.

blocks.title: Hunger becomes a desire to eat
blocks.text: The same physically. Because of the body's makeup, the soul's desire to express itself freely in the body, once enclothed there, becomes associated with the desire to eat and drink. Then the desire to stop the pain in the stomach when hungry becomes a desire to eat, since you learn that eating takes the pain away and gives strength; feeling weak or hungry right away creates a desire for food. That is not the essential desire, it is created; but once associated, the one reveals the other. That is *gilui ha'helem*.

phrases.he: ומובן על כל פנים שיש הפרש גדול בין גלוי הרצון לחסד, שאינו רק בחינת גלוי ההעלם של עצם הרצון, המוליד רצון זה
phrases.en: So from this we understand there's a big difference between the *ratzon* that's born out as a *gilui* from the *etzem ratzon* and the *etzem ratzon*.

phrases.he: שהוא בא מכח עצם המדה, שהוא אינו בחינת נבדל כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: **So from this we understand there's a big difference between the *ratzon* that's born out as a *gilui* from the *etzem ratzon* and the *etzem ratzon***, which comes from the power of the essence of the attribute and is not a separate thing. The will that comes out is detached from your essence: you do not really want it. The essential will you really want.

blocks.title: I never wanted to drive
blocks.text: A guy is hungry, with a whole plan: get pizza, get in his car and drive. He is putting his shoes on when a guy walks in: "Look, I brought pizza." He starts taking his shoes off. "I thought you wanted to drive to the store and everything." "No, no, I never wanted it at all."

That is the meaning of the world being created *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing): the external things of the world are not really what G-d wants at all. You do not have to do anything to stop him wanting to drive down the block; he wanted it only because it was connected to what he did want. Take the connection away and the desire vanishes at once, because it never had its own *metzius* (existence).

That itself is the point of *davenen* (praying): to show your *nefesh habehamis* (animal soul) that what it really wants, if it goes back to its essential desire, requires connecting to G-d. Most people are not conscious of this. That is the problem: a person associates a certain form with what he wants and gets stuck in it; if it does not work out, he is disappointed, and forgets it was not really what he wanted.

This can happen because a person really can choose to want whatever he wants. He could make something that is normally a *prat* (a detail) his essential goal. It is not his inner essence, but he has *bechira* (free choice). Once he has a *kavana* (intention), he makes a hierarchy of his inner will and his external will.

With people's problems you always have to do both, the *naaseh* side and the *nishma* side ("we will do" and "we will understand"). Having people refine from scratch their view of what they want is *is'hapcha* (transforming the feeling itself): it actually changes their desire. That is the real meaning of *moach shalit al halev*, the mind rules the heart: change what you associate a thing with and your feeling about it changes automatically, because the feeling is a born will that comes from your essential will through your *sechel*, which makes the associations.

But until a person can do that, he has to start with *iskafya* (forcing oneself against the feeling), and it has a *maala* (advantage) too; that is the idea of *Pada b'shalom nafshi mikrav li*. If the whole thing were to realize the truth, be inspired and be a *tzaddik* (righteous man), *Hashem* could have made us *tzaddikim*. But He also wants *avoda* (divine service), work. So there is always a level we enjoy and one we do not, and at any level there is an *iskafya* to do. *Hashem* made you not feel like doing things to give you a meaningful relationship: making yourself do what you do not feel like doing, to connect to G-d, is meaningful because you are actually giving something up.

That is the *naaseh*, and it is a prerequisite: the willingness to push a little is what makes the *nishma* possible afterwards. So first he makes *hachlatos* (resolutions) to do the external things *halacha* asks: make sure the place is nice, stand nicely, look in the *Siddur*, not talk during *davenen*, not take his *tefillin* off early. Trying to get out early will mess it up. Make an effort even when you do not feel like it, like finishing *Tehillim* before you take your *tefillin* off, whatever shows you are making this a priority. Then you have to start to understand and appreciate what is going on when you are *davenen*.

sections.title: Atzilus called out from Adam Kadmon: lights, Moshe's spirit, the Kesarim
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are only what was hidden in *Adam Kadmon* coming out, so they are called lights, like the spirit drawn off Moshe onto the elders without his losing any. Their *Kesarim* are revealed wills, like the will to give a poor man a dollar, which *Adam Kadmon* ties to the essential will.

phrases.he: ועל דרך משל זה יובן ענין קורא הדורות מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
כמשל הקורא דבר שיצא מהעלמו לגלוי לחוץ
כך כל עיקר בחינת עשר ספירות דאצילות הוא שיצאו מהעלמם לגלוי בלבד
phrases.en: the whole *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* is that they were *b'helem* in *Adam Kadmon*, and now they're just coming out *b'gilui*.

phrases.he: ועל כן נקראו בשם אורות או ספירות,
phrases.en: That's why what comes out in *Atzilus* is called *oros*, or *sefiros*,

phrases.he: כמו זיו ואור

blocks.text: By this *mashal* we can understand *kore hadoros meirosh* of *Adam Kadmon*: like calling a thing out of hiding into the open, as if a guy were hiding behind a curtain and you said, "Okay, come out now." So **the whole *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* is that they were *b'helem* in *Adam Kadmon*, and now they're just coming out *b'gilui***.

Once *Hashem* had the essential wills for the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), the *igul* of *Adam Kadmon*, He made in *Adam Kadmon* the general image of what fulfils them. Then, when a particular situation comes up, the particular will, the Torah and *mitzvos*, how *Hashem* wants you to act here, comes *mimeila* (by itself): *Adam Kadmon* already made the association with the essential will, and the situation only reveals what was decided there.

**That's why what comes out in *Atzilus* is called *oros*, or *sefiros***, like radiance and light: only a revelation of the *etzem*. *Adam Kadmon* is like the *Maor*, the *etzem*, and what comes in *Atzilus* is only its revelation. *Atzilus* is that *Hashem* is going to reveal Himself as creating a world.

Say the *chesed* of *Arich* is the light of the *chesed* of *Atzilus*. It is that everything *Hashem* creates is recreated by Him every moment, because He is the true *metzius* and everything depends on Him. That a created thing must be recreated every second is a *gilui* of the essential thing, which is like *Adam Kadmon*: *Hashem* decided there to reveal Himself as a creator, and not just a creator but the ultimate creator, essentially a creator.

To be essentially a creator means that everything that exists depends totally on Him. That our world is created by Him every moment is a *gilui* of that, not the G-dliness itself, a symptom: a world created every moment tells you its relationship to its Creator, and so tells you something about the Creator.

phrases.he: וכמו כל בחינת גלוי ההעלם שאינו רק בבחינת אור, וכבחינת מראה וגוון,
וכמו תנועת החי כו'
phrases.en: like the movement of a living thing reveals that it's alive.

phrases.he: והיינו כמו ויאצל מן הרוח,
phrases.en: this is like it says by Moshe, that *Hashem* took some of Moshe's spirit and put it on the seventy *zekeinim*.

phrases.he: שאין זה רוחו של משה
phrases.en: this is not Moshe's actual *ruach*, it's not like he lost his *ruach*,

phrases.he: רק בחינת גלוי אורו וזיוו לבד, הוא שנאצל והופרש, כגלוי שלהבת מן הגחלת וכהאי גוונא כו'

blocks.text: Revealing the hidden is only like light and color: **like the movement of a living thing reveals that it's alive**. Hence the name *Atzilus*, from *vayatzel min haruach*: **this is like it says by Moshe, that *Hashem* took some of Moshe's spirit and put it on the seventy *zekeinim*** (elders). **This is not Moshe's actual *ruach*, it's not like he lost his *ruach***; only his light was drawn off, like a flame from the coal, or Rashi's candle that lights others and loses none of its flame.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's shluchim
blocks.text: When the Rebbe sends out *shluchim* (emissaries), they have a little of the Rebbe's *ruach*: they go with his ideology. The more they make themselves *batel* (nullified) to his will, the more successful they are, because the Rebbe knows what he is doing, sees things a lot better than we do, and knows the actual reality: what everything is for and what is supposed to be going on. You do not have to become Moshe. Nullify yourself to his will, and you reveal his *ruach*.

blocks.title: A conduit for G-d's wisdom
blocks.text: The same with a person who learns Torah. It is really G-d's wisdom, not his. But if he works to understand it, to make himself just understand what G-d is saying, people will think he is very smart. It is not his own thing; he just became a better conduit for it.

So too *Hashem* made the elders conduits to Moshe's *ruach*: He opened them up to see better, with a little of Moshe's *ruach hakodesh* (holy spirit), his *nevua* (prophecy), so that they were able to know the truth for being judges.

phrases.he: וכל זה יובן על פי משל הנזכר לעיל מענין גלוי הרצון בדבר נבדל
phrases.en: So this is all like the *mashal* of the *gilui ratzon*,

phrases.he: שיוצא מהעלם עצם הרצון שמצד עצמיות כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which comes out from the *etzem haratzon*, which is that a person's essential bias comes from his essential character.

phrases.he: כך בחינת כתרים דעשר ספירות דאצילות הן רק בחינת גלוי רצון לגבי העלם עצם הרצון שנקרא רצון לרצון,
שהוא בבחינת אדם קדמון כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: **So this is all like the *mashal* of the *gilui ratzon*** in a separate thing, **which comes out from the *etzem haratzon*, which is that a person's essential bias comes from his essential character**. So the *Kesarim* (crowns) of *Atzilus* are only a revealed will, compared with the hidden *ratzon l'ratzon* (a will for a will). The will of *Atzilus* is particular, like wanting to give a poor person a dollar. The *ratzon l'ratzon* in *Adam Kadmon* is the bias that counts this as nice and so ties it to the will for *chesed*, and to the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will), the *igulim* before *Adam Kadmon*.

So if a person wants *chesed*, and *Adam Kadmon* tells him this is connected, he will want this. In the same way, *Hashem*'s decision to want a *dira b'tachtonim* in a certain order makes the Torah. The *chachma* (wisdom) of the Torah is to be *batel* to *Adam Kadmon*: to tell you accurately, in each situation, what brings you closer to the *dira b'tachtonim* and what farther away.

If *Hashem* decided He wants the *dira* another way, the revealed will would change automatically. Certain things *Hashem* said will not change, and that is why they cannot. But essentially, putting on *tefillin* is not good and not putting them on bad: *Hashem* decided He wants it, so now it is connected to G-d, and so now it is good.

phrases.he: וכמו מבחינת העלם הרצון דחסד דאדם קדמון נמשך גלוי רצון לחסד דאצילות שנקרא כתר דחסד כו'
וכן מבחינת העלם רצון דחכמה כו'
phrases.en: from the *etzem ratzon* of *chachma* comes the *chachma* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: As from the hidden will for *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon* is drawn the revealed will for *chesed* of *Atzilus*, the *Keser* of *chesed*. *Hashem*'s decision to reveal Himself as a creator became a will to create our world, only one example of it; creating it is not the essential thing. What reveals the *etzem*, that He is a creator, is that He creates it every moment, all the time.

And so from the hidden will for *chachma*: **from the *etzem ratzon* of *chachma* comes the *chachma* of *Atzilus***. Since *Hashem* wanted to reveal Himself as wise, He had a will in *Atzilus* to have wisdom in the world and in the Torah. And so when we look around the world, we see a lot of wisdom in it.

sections.title: From Malchus of Adam Kadmon to the Keser of Atzilus: the giver's speech becomes the receiver's will
sections.summary: Only the outer expression, the *Malchus*, of each level becomes the *Keser* of the next: a person's self-image measures each situation, the king's spoken wish becomes the servant's own will, and the teacher's words become the student's understanding. So the external letters of *Adam Kadmon* define *Atik* and *Arich*, and all of history is chosen from what is in *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: אך כמו שמובן ממשל הנזכר לעיל שזהו הנקרא התהוות רצון לרצון,
הרי הוא בא בבחינת הכלל
phrases.en: so it's like a *klal*,

phrases.he: להוליד כמה מיני רצון וכמה ענינים אופנים שונים כו',
phrases.en: and includes many particular things: whatever each circumstance, that inner *etzem ratzon* to be kind will come out in different ways.

phrases.he: כך מבחינת רצון לרצון לחסד באדם קדמון נולד כמה מיני גלוי רצון של חסד באצילות
phrases.en: So too, the *etzem ratzon* for *chesed* comes out in many different particular *inyanim* in *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: But as is now understood, this is called a *ratzon l'ratzon*. *Adam Kadmon* is the general will for everything you will ever do, **so it's like a *klal*** (a general whole), **and includes many particular things: whatever each circumstance, that inner *etzem ratzon* to be kind will come out in different ways**. **So too, the *etzem ratzon* for *chesed* comes out in many different particular *inyanim* in *Atzilus*.**

phrases.he: והענין הוא דמבחינת המלכות של מדה דאדם קדמון נעשה בחינת כתר דמדה דאצילות
phrases.en: from the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: ובכללות העשר ספירות הרי רק מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר דאצילות
והוא רק מבחינת אותיות וגלוי עצם העלם הרצון, נעשה אור העצם של גלוי רצון כו'
(שהוא כמו שמבואר באות הי''ח
דרק מבחינת סוף מעשה דעצם הרצון נעשה רצון לרצון שהוא עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון)
phrases.en: only from *Malchus* of the *igulim* becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*,

blocks.title: The self-image of a talmid chacham
blocks.text: The matter is that **from the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus***. The *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* is the external form, something definable. Say a person has a clear self-image of what he wants, whispering in his ear that he wants to be, say, a *talmid chacham* (a Torah scholar). Its *Malchus* is the whole picture, the whole *hanhaga* (conduct), of what it means to be a guy like that. In every situation he measures against it: "Well, does this fit with this form?" If it fits, he has a will for it; if not, a will against it. That creates the *Keser* of his particular things, like the *Keser* of *Atzilus*.

It is only from the letters and the revealing of the hidden essential will that the essential light of the revealed will comes into being, as was explained in section 18: only from the last level of the deed of the essential will comes the *ratzon l'ratzon*, the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*. Just as **only from *Malchus* of the *igulim* becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon***, so too only from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* comes *Keser* of *Atzilus*. Now he is going to give us a *mashal* for this.

phrases.he: (על דרך דוגמא, מגלוי רצון שבדבור המשפיע נעשה עצם הרצון למקבל
כמו שמאותיות גלוי השכל שבדבור שבמשפיע נעשה עצם אור השכל במקבל
phrases.en: How the students get their *sechel* from the letters of the teacher.

phrases.he: וכך רק מאותיות וגלוי חסד שבדבור דמשפיע נעשה אור הרצון לחסד למקבל
כידוע בכל עילה ועלול,
phrases.en: this is the way it works in every *ila v'alul*,

phrases.he: שמבחינת האחרונה שבעילה נעשה ראש ושרש לעלול
phrases.en: That his *chitzoniyus* becomes your *pnimiyus*.

blocks.title: Your wish is my command
blocks.text: By way of example: from the will revealed in the speech of the *mashpia* (the giver) comes the essential will of the *mekabel* (the receiver). The servant tells the king, "Your wish is my command." His will is really for the *baal haratzon*, the one whose will it is. So how does he know what to want? Whatever the king tells him, the external revealing of the king's will, becomes his will.

That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): when you give over the point of your will, anything he tells you to do automatically becomes your full inner will. The particular thing is not the essential will, but since he said to do it, it gets the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*. If a person tried to stop you, "you would die or kill him or whatever to not let him stop you."

sensitivity.reason: Says that with mesirus nefesh a servant would kill a person who tried to stop him carrying out the order; out of context it reads as approving violence.
sensitivity.publishable: That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): when you give over the point of your will, anything he tells you to do automatically becomes your full inner will. The particular thing is not the essential will, but since he said to do it, it gets the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*. Nothing anyone did could stop you.

blocks.title: The student and the teacher
blocks.text: The same with a teacher: as from the letters of the intellect revealed in the giver's speech comes the essential light of the receiver's intellect, **how the students get their *sechel* from the letters of the teacher**. The students essentially want to learn whatever this guy knows: they believe he is an expert with something they do not know, and so whatever he says, they accept as true.

To really learn properly you have to be *batel* and accept, even when you do not understand, that he knows better than you, and just try to understand what he is saying. If you allow that maybe he is wrong, you might not understand it properly; then it does not make sense, so you say it is not true. Knowing that he knows is what guarantees you will understand it properly.

And so only from the kindness revealed in the giver's speech comes the will for kindness in the receiver. If a person loves somebody who praises someone else, he will love that one too, because he trusts him. Praise can also wake up love in the one who says it, but here it is said to another. As is known, **this is the way it works in every *ila v'alul***: the last level of the cause becomes the head and root of the effect. **His *chitzoniyus* becomes your *pnimiyus*** (his outside becomes your inside).

phrases.he: וכך מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון בכלל נעשה בחינת כתר דעתיק יומין כו'
phrases.en: the whole thing of *Atik* and *Arich* is defined based on the external *osios* of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: דהיינו מבחינת גלוי רצון לרצון שבדבור בלבד,
נעשה בחינת מקור כל גלוי רצון שמצד התענוג שנקרא כתר דעתיק יומין כו' וכמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: And so from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* comes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*: **the whole thing of *Atik* and *Arich* is defined based on the external *osios* of *Adam Kadmon*** (its letters), from the revealing of the *ratzon l'ratzon* in speech alone. *Hashem* chooses which part of it comes out now. That is *kore hadoros meirosh*: He picks which generation comes out now, and that choice makes the way all the wills come out.

It becomes the source of every revealed will that comes from the *taanug* (delight), the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*. A person enjoys something when he sees it fulfilling his self-image; if he sees it as against his self-image, he hates it. What *ratzon* and *taanug* are is learned later, but it is the same way with G-d.

phrases.he: והיינו כללות ענין העשר ספירות דאצילות שיצאו מהעלם עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, כמו שכתוב קורא הדורות מראש כו':
phrases.en: That's the *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, that they are only a *gilui* of the *etzem* thing of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: And this is the whole matter of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, which came out of the concealment of the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*: *kore hadoros meirosh*. **That's the *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, that they are only a *gilui* of the *etzem* thing of *Adam Kadmon*.** In *Adam Kadmon* *Hashem* chose the essential form in which He wants to reveal Himself in this world, the ten *sefiros* in general in a certain form.

It is also the form of *Moshiach* and of the *dira b'tachtonim* that *Hashem* chose. That defines how He conducts the world all the time, depending on which aspect of *Adam Kadmon* He is revealing now; the whole of history is defined by it. That is why *nevua* is possible: if you know the story in *Adam Kadmon*, you know how it will come out down the line.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between *etzem v'hispashtus* and *gilui ha'helem*, and how do the sunlight in a room and the sun seen through the window show both?
Why are movement, speech and the color of an apple truer *meshalim* for *gilui ha'helem* than the flame hidden in a coal?
How do you know that a person is kind or cruel, and why can a single act, like tying a man to a bench and cutting him, not tell you?
What does the man who takes his shoes back off when the pizza arrives show about the born will, and what does it teach about the world and about *davenen*?
Why are the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* called lights, and what does Moshe's spirit placed on the seventy elders show about them?
How does the servant who says "Your wish is my command" explain that only the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus*?

notes.text: Lines 1 and 2 are read at the start of class 66 without a rendering; his next sentences describe the chapter's subject (how the lights of Atzilus come out from Adam Kadmon) rather than translate the lines, so those phrases keep their Hebrew alone. Other phrases he reads without translating: the first half of line 3, the end of line 7, line 9, the end of lines 10 and 12, the end of line 13 ("v'kayadua"), the second half of line 14, lines 15, 22 and the start of 23, the end of line 24 ("shehu talui b'etzem hamidda tamid"), the end of line 25, the end of line 17, the first half of line 18, the end of line 26, line 31, lines 32-33 (for line 33 he gives the curtain mashal, not a rendering), the end of line 35, the start of line 36, line 38, line 41, line 42, the start of line 44, lines 47, 49 and 51, the start of line 48, line 46 (not read), line 54, and the words "v'amar b'Sefer Yetzira" of line 5.
Line 10 is read at 67 w118-134 without a rendering; its phrases cite his second reading of it later in the class, where he translates it (67 w1481-1515 and w1605-1621).

Line 46 is not read aloud. His sentence at 71 w347-369 ("Just like only from Malchus of the igulim becomes Keser of A"K, so too only from Malchus of A"K comes Keser of Atzilus") follows his reading of line 48; its first half is the en of line 48's second phrase. Its second half restates lines 45-46, but since he never reads line 46, line 46's phrase has no en (review change); the sentence is in the explanation block.
Lines 27-29 are not read in any class: class 69 goes from line 26 to a long explanation and then reads line 30. They are kept as a no-recording passage.

The man "tied down to a bench and cut up" (68 w867-955) is not explained in class 68; in class 69 (w497-519, w672-694) he names the surgeon and the will "to cut somebody" as a will that only its association can show to be chesed. The block keeps the riddle as he posed it and the surgeon in the block where he says it; it was not flagged, since the point is the surgeon. A reviewer may want a flag for the image.

Sources as he gives them: the maamar Sachar Oscha in the Siddur, with Reb Hillel's commentary on it; "I think" a number of maamarim at the beginning of Ayin Beis based on Imrei Bina (67 w1315-1373); Chinuch Lanaar, which he first ascribes to the Frierdiker Rebbe and then corrects to the Rebbe Rashab (68 w1373-1428); Rashi's candle on vayatzel (70 w632-663). Kept as said; not checked.

At 69 w1510 he says "Yeah, well, that's the thing. You always have to do both with people, with anytime when people have these kind of problems", as if answering someone; no question is heard on the tape (the series has no audible students). Written as part of the avodah block, not as a question. The block does not quote "Yeah, well, that's the thing" (review change).

Class 69 ends mid-sentence ("what's going on when you're davenen, and"), and class 70 does not resume the point. Class 69's long avodah on davenen (w1311-2123) belongs to no line; it is placed under lines 30-31, which it follows.
The transcript hears line 53's "Keser d'Atik Yomin" once as "כתר דעקודים" (71 w979-988 and w1081-1094); the chapter's text is followed.
"Pada b'shalom nafshi mikrav li" (69 w1678-1737) is named but he does not say how it applies before going on to iskafya; the block keeps only the mention.

Review: the four sensitivity flags were kept. The church-and-state digression's publishable text now keeps the Rebbe's sicha on teaching morality, dropping only the political dispute. The "liberal" aside is a borderline flag (a political label used as an example, not an opinion), kept since a flag costs nothing. Line 55's block was a recap; it explains the line in class order, so it is now an explanation.
